explanation: A skeleton found soon after Darwin published On the Origin of Species made it famous evidence that birds evolved from small, dinosaur-like reptiles.

claims.text: Archaeopteryx fossils from Germany show feathered wings together with teeth and a long bony tail.
Pterodactyls, Iguanodon and ichthyosaurs did not have feathered wings.
An Archaeopteryx skeleton was found soon after Darwin published On the Origin of Species.
Archaeopteryx became famous evidence that birds evolved from dinosaur-like reptiles.

evidence.restatement: Archaeopteryx fossils from the Solnhofen limestone of Germany show feathered wings together with teeth and a long bony tail.
Pterosaurs such as pterodactyls had membrane wings, ichthyosaurs had flippers and Iguanodon had no wings; none had feathered wings.
The first Archaeopteryx skeleton came to light in 1861, two years after On the Origin of Species appeared in 1859.
Archaeopteryx became a famous transitional fossil linking birds with dinosaur-like reptiles.
